summary: We are testing whether an FM (Fiduccia-Mattheyses) partitioning algorithm with greedy local search and random restarts can achieve a high Max-Cut score (predicted >85/100) on problem #192, compared to a trivial alternating baseline (predicted ~50/100). This validates that the FM escape-from-local-optima mechanism is the key driver of performance.
key_points: h-main: FM partitioning with greedy local search init, FM passes (best-prefix vertex-flip sequences), and multiple random restarts within a 0.90s time budget. Predicted score >85.
h-control-negative: Trivial s[i] = i%2 assignment ignoring graph structure. Predicted score ~50, establishing a lower bound to confirm the FM mechanism matters.

Confirmation criteria: h-main scores significantly above h-control-negative (ideally >85 vs ~50). Refutation: if h-main scores ≤60 or h-control-negative scores unexpectedly high (>75), indicating either FM isn't helping or the problem structure makes any assignment work well.
Key risk: the 1s time limit per test case — the 0.90s budget leaves only 0.10s margin. If FM restarts are too slow for n=1000, m=20000 graphs, score could drop to 0 on large cases.
Output format is critical: exactly one line of n space-separated 0/1 values. Any deviation (extra newlines, wrong separators) could zero the score regardless of algorithmic quality.
